tagline.text: A mid-market BGC mall with an open-air Fiesta Market

children.text: Market! Market! is a large Ayala Malls shopping center that opened in 2004 and is a rare mid-market mall inside BGC. With fresh fruit and street food at the Fiesta Market out front and bus terminals in and around the mall, it makes a handy base for a day out in BGC.

Market! Market! is a large shopping mall on McKinley Parkway in Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Taguig, Metro Manila. Ayala Land built it on land leased from the government's Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), and it opened on September 16, 2004. The site covers about 9.7 hectares (24 acres), and the mall is said to hold more than 520 stores and services across five upper floors and one basement level. It also stands on the former site of General Douglas MacArthur's staff house, which is a fun detail to know.

Its defining trait is that it targets middle-income and everyday shoppers in a district known for its upscale image. Unlike most other Ayala malls, which aim at wealthier customers, Market! Market! mixes mainstream brands, outlet and bargain stores, themed bazaars and open-air stalls. As the name suggests, it brings the feel of a traditional Filipino marketplace into a modern mall. The highlight is the open-air Fiesta Market across from the main entrance, where you can buy fresh fruit, vegetables, seafood, Filipino street food and pasalubong (souvenir gifts).

It is also an important transport hub. Inside and around the mall are the BGC bus terminal and stands for jeepneys and UV Express vans, and routes toward Alabang, Laguna and Batangas depart from here. That makes it a convenient stop on the way to BGC or Makati for lunch, money changing, grocery shopping or a movie. It is less a tourist sight than a lifestyle destination where you can see everyday local life up close.

The mall's future is worth watching as well. According to September 2026 reports, the BCDA and the operator agreed to extend the lease by 12 years and 7 months starting June 2027, and the operator plans to invest about 1 billion pesos to renovate the mall. The planned BGC station of the Metro Manila Subway is also to be linked to the site. Construction timing and scope may change, so please check the latest announcements before you visit.

This open-air area across from the main entrance offers fresh fruit, vegetables, seafood and street food all in one place. Many visitors say the fruit is cheaper than at supermarkets, so it is a good place to try tropical fruit. Prices and stalls change often, so confirm on site.

Fashion, accessories, electronics and household goods, plus outlet and bargain stores, are mixed across the floors. Metro Department Store and the Home Market area also offer home decor. It is easy to browse slowly and compare prices.

On the ground floor you will find Lord Stow's Bakery (known for its egg tarts since 1999), Ikkoryu Fukuoka Ramen, Popeyes, Tim Hortons, Banapple and more. The fourth floor has steak and Japanese restaurants, and Syano Resto Grill serves dishes from different regions of the Philippines. Check the floor directories to choose.
The fifth floor has seven cinemas. They are a cool refuge on a hot day or a rainy afternoon. Check showtimes and seats in the cinema app or at the box office.

The mall hosts themed bazaars, food festivals, concerts and mall tours. On weekends, handicraft and food markets sometimes set up. Schedules differ every time, so check the mall's official announcements.

BGC Bus (East, West and Central routes), buses to Alabang, Laguna and Batangas, jeepneys and UV Express vans all pass through here. It sits on a gateway into BGC from all sides of Manila, which suits travelers using public transport.
The garden area in front of the entrance, a children's play area and kiddie rides suit travelers with kids. On Sundays at 11 a.m., Mass is held in the C5 Wing on the ground floor.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Fiesta Market and a lap of the mall

children.text: Arrive when the mall opens at
. First walk around the garden and Fiesta Market, compare fruit prices and try one or two things you like.
Work your way up slowly from the ground floor, browsing the stores. If you need money changed, a pharmacy or a SIM card, this is a good time.
Eat lunch at the ground-floor food outlets or the fourth-floor restaurants. Well-known names like Ikkoryu Fukuoka Ramen or Lord Stow's egg tarts are good picks.
Watch a movie at the fifth-floor cinema or rest at a cafe.
Leave before rush hour by BGC Bus or taxi. Roads around BGC are very congested on weekday evenings.
Market! Market! fits well into a BGC itinerary. If you also want to see Bonifacio High Street or BGC's street art the same day, plan the mall in the morning and the street walk in the afternoon.

items.title: Transit route
items.subtitle: Using it as a gateway into BGC

children.text: Early in the morning, take a BGC bus or direct bus from Alabang or Laguna and get off at the Market! Market! terminal.
When the mall opens, sort out your bags and have a light brunch.
Take the BGC Bus Central route or similar to the center of BGC. Resting inside the mall before you move helps you avoid the heat.
A Grab or taxi from the airport (NAIA) takes about
40 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes
depending on traffic. Enter 'Market! Market!, McKinley Parkway, Taguig' as the destination.
You can also head to nearby PITX or FTI and switch to a jeepney or UV Express, but a Grab is easier with luggage.
During rush hour (weekdays
and
), travel time increases greatly.
You can take a jeepney marked "Market Market" from the terminal under Ayala MRT station in Makati. It takes about
20–40 minutes
depending on road conditions.
BGC Bus East, West and Central routes depart from the Market! Market! terminal, and the regular fare is around ₱15 (varies by route).
Jeepneys and FX/UV Express vans leave from the north terminal (near Metro Department Store) and the south terminal (near Fiesta Market).
From Guadalupe MRT station, a jeepney bound for AFP Housing or Gate 3 passes the mall. UV Express vans also serve Antipolo, Imus, Pasig and Rosario.
Long-distance buses toward Alabang, Laguna, Batangas and Bicol are listed, but timetables change often, so check on-site information.
Set the main entrance of 'Market! Market!' as your Grab destination. There are two parking areas, an open lot near Fiesta Market and a car park building near BPI, both listed as open 24 hours.
Parking was reported in 2020 at about ₱50 for the first 3 hours and about ₱15 per additional hour; no current official rate was found, so confirm on site.

Market! Market! mixes an indoor mall with an outdoor market, so you can visit year-round. However, the outdoor Fiesta Market is very hot at midday and gets wet in the rainy season, so choose your timing.

Weekday mornings are relatively quiet, while weekends, holidays and the Christmas season are crowded. Around Christmas, extra temporary stalls are reported to appear outdoors, which adds energy but makes getting around harder.

There is no lodging inside Market! Market!, but BGC within walking distance has many mid-range hotels and serviced residences. Staying in BGC keeps the mall and restaurants close, which suits shopping and food plans. Prices vary greatly by season and booking site, so compare.

For food, choosing long-established well-known places lowers the risk of disappointment. On the ground floor are Lord Stow's Bakery with its Portuguese-style egg tarts, Ikkoryu Fukuoka Ramen, Tim Hortons, Banapple and Popeyes. For something light, try grilled fish, street skewers or seasonal fruit at Fiesta Market.
Hours are listed as
on weekdays and

on weekends and holidays in some guides, while the official Ayala Malls listing says daily 10:00–22:00, so sources differ. Hours can also change on holidays, so check the mall's official channels before visiting.
It is very crowded on weekends and around payday. For a relaxed visit, go on a weekday morning.
Many Fiesta Market items have no price tags, so ask before buying, and buy fruit in small amounts to taste first.
When taking the BGC Bus, check the route (East, West, Central) and stop in advance. Keep small bills or change ready.
Jeepney and UV Express terminals are split between the north and south sides, so go to the stand that matches your route.
On Sundays at
, Mass is held on the ground floor of the C5 Wing. The area can be busy then.
If you bring a pet into the mall, there are rules to carry it and keep it clean, so check before you go.
Construction around BGC sometimes changes routes. Check the current entrance in your map app before heading over.
A mall renovation and subway station construction are planned, so entrances and terminal locations may change. Check the latest announcements before you visit.
Watch for pickpockets on crowded weekends and at year-end, and carry your bag in front.
Fiesta Market is outdoors and vulnerable to heat and sudden showers. Bring water, an umbrella and a hat.
Check hygiene by eye for street food and be careful with ice and raw items.
Avoid taxis or money changers from touts without official guidance, and use an official exchange counter inside the mall.
